text:
josh: Quick question — how do we want to attribute token costs when routing + cache interact? We had a customer report where a request routed to main-model, missed prefix cache, then fell back to tiny-quant which produced most tokens. Who gets the cache credit and how do we show it in the console?

megan: my take: cache hits should give a "credit" to the original route (the one that would have handled it) so that the route's effective unit-cost drops. If fallback produces tokens, bill them to the route that actually executed. Problem is when fallback crosses tenant/policy boundaries.

tariq: agree on the credits idea. Practically we need a clear event model: emit a single terminal telemetry event per request that includes: origin_route, executing_route, cache_hit boolean, prefix_hit_tokens, generated_tokens, model_used, cost_microcents. That lets downstream billing rollups decide.

liz: small UX ask — in the console we'd show: 1) nominal per-token rate of the pinned model, 2) cache credits applied (tokens and $), 3) delta from fallback. Customers keep asking for the "why did my cost spike" view.

kevin: edge case: streaming where first chunks come from cache and later the model generates new tokens after fallback. We need to ensure attribution for streamed tokens is ordered. I think we should attribute tokens to the executing route at the moment they were produced. Means telemetry must record token-level slices or at least two events (cache_hit slice + generation slice).

josh: good point. Can't explode the event volume though. Proposal: emit up to two events per request: one for prefix/cache hit (if any) and one for generation. Each event has tokens and unit cost. Billing joins by request_id.

megan: +1. Also we should surface a "cache credit" column in the per-route chargeback report that is computed as sum(prefix_tokens * model_unit_cost_of_route) so you can see recovered dollars.

tariq: here's a suggested telemetry proto in plain text for reviewers:```
{
  request_id: "r_...",
  origin_route: "tenant/foo/route/bar",
  executing_route: "tenant/foo/route/bar" | "fallback/quant-4bit",
  model: "redwood/gptx-13b-q4",
  event_type: "prefix_hit" | "generation",
  tokens: 42,
  unit_cost_microcents: 12,
  cache_origin: "kv-cache" | null
}
``` This keeps it simple and joinable.

liz: can we also include a boolean "cross_tenant" when routing can cross tenants (for shared fallback pools)? important for chargeback decisions.

kevin: quotas comment — if a tenant has route-level quota, do we decrement quota on origin_route or executing_route? For fairness quota should be decremented on the origin_route (so callers can't evade quotas via fallback). But for capacity accounting we should attribute compute to executing_route.

josh: sounds like we need two orthogonal attributions: billing attribution (based on executing events + credits) and quota enforcement (charged on origin). Need doc + small diagram in console help.

megan: UX rollout: expose an "attribution mode" toggle for admins: "credit-to-origin" vs "bill-to-executing" with a short tooltip. Default to credits-to-origin with fallback billed to executing.

ops-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/3281 - "token-attribution: event model + console UX" and assigned to @tariq + @megan.

tariq: I'll draft the PR for telemetry schema + a small SQL rollup view that computes: total_billed = sum(generation.tokens * generation.unit_cost) - sum(prefix.tokens * origin_unit_cost) per route. Share later.

josh: cool. One last nit — rounding. Use microcents to avoid float drift and only round at final invoice level. Keep rollups in integers.

kevin: noted. Also suggest a quick smoke dashboard: show "unattributed delta" where billed != expected_by_route so ops can flag weird routing loops.

megan: that's it from me. I'll update the console mockups with a cache-credit column and a tooltip example.

josh: thanks all. We'll review the telemetry PR next week in eng-platform sync. :thumbsup:
